title: Sources, Transfers & Sinks
welcome_lead: Map sediment flows in a UK cell.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on coastal sediment cells, sources, transfers and sinks.
final_note: Cells are largely closed sediment compartments.

concepts.def: Self-contained coastal compartment for sediment movement.
Sediment input: cliffs, rivers, offshore sources, biological.
Movement via waves, longshore drift, tidal currents.
Where sediment is deposited: spits, bars, offshore.
Major UK source: Holderness contributes ~2 million m^3/yr.
River-supplied sediment; reduced by dams and abstraction.

walkthroughs.body_html: Holderness cliffs (boulder clay) supply ~2 million m^3/yr. Rivers Tees and Humber add fluvial sediment. Offshore banks (e.g. Dogger Bank) supplied during last glaciation contribute via wave action. Biological sources (shell debris) are locally important.

Longshore drift dominates: oblique swash up beach, gravity backwash perpendicular. Atlantic swell drives drift along south coast (W to E typical). Tidal currents move suspended fines. Storms cause offshore transport then summer recovery.

Spurn Head (5.5 km recurved spit) is the major sink for Cell 2. Offshore deeper than 10 m generally permanent loss. Salt marshes (Essex coast) trap fine sediment. Estuarine sinks (Thames, Humber) accumulate fluvial and marine sediment.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.

mcqs.q: Why do some rivers form deltas and others form estuaries?
options: The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
Deltas form where rivers deposit sediment faster than the sea can remove it (calm seas, heavy load); estuaries form where tidal energy removes sediment (strong tides).
Deltas form on big rivers and estuaries on small ones.
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
